manifest.name: Greenhollow Vale
manifest.author: Greenhollow
manifest.description: The base game: the village of Greenhollow, its people, wildlife and materials.

items.name: Iron Ingot
items.description: A bar of bloomery iron. Soft, forgiving and cheap.

items.name: Steel Ingot
items.description: Carefully carburised steel. Holds an edge far longer than iron.

items.name: Bronze Ingot
items.description: Heavy and easy to work, though it dulls quickly.

items.name: Iron Ore
items.description: Rust-red ore from the Greyback slopes. Bram pays fair coin for it.

items.name: Healing Draught
items.description: Mira's yarrow tincture. Bitter, but it closes wounds.

items.name: Mind Tonic
items.description: A pale blue tonic that clears the head.

items.name: Barley Loaf
items.description: Dense, dark and filling.

items.name: Stag Stew
items.description: The Gilded Stag's famous supper.

items.name: Orchard Apple
items.description: Crisp and a little sour.

items.name: Venison
items.description: A good cut. Better cooked.

items.name: River Trout
items.description: Fresh from the Silverrun.

items.name: Wolf Pelt
items.description: Thick grey fur. The tailor will want it.

items.name: Deer Hide
items.description: Supple hide, good for jerkins.

items.name: Boar Tusk
items.description: Yellowed ivory, sharp as a nail.

items.name: Yarrow Sprig
items.description: White flowers that staunch bleeding.

items.name: Rough Amethyst
items.description: A cloudy violet stone prised from the hills.

items.name: Bedroll
items.description: Wool and waxed canvas.

items.name: Coin Pouch
items.description: Leather, drawstring, mostly empty.

items.name: Hemp Rope
items.description: Ten paces of good rope.

items.name: Annals of the Vale
items.description: A worn chronicle of the vale, kept by the first innkeeper of the Gilded Stag.
items.text:
Greenhollow was founded beneath the white ash by seven families fleeing the Greyback mines. They brought picks, seed barley and one anvil, and swore never again to dig for another man's profit.

The ash still marks every door. When a child of the vale comes of age, a leaf is pressed into the lintel of the house they were born in.

Of the old mines little is written, save that the deepest gallery was sealed in a single night and that nobody who did the sealing would say why.

items.name: Ironwood Longsword
items.description: An iron blade on an ironwood grip. Honest work.

items.name: Hunting Knife
items.description: Short, quick and always sharp.

items.name: Forged Blade
items.description: A blade shaped by your own hammer.

items.name: Leather Cap
items.description: Boiled leather, stitched twice.

items.name: Padded Jerkin
items.description: Quilted linen that turns a glancing bite.

items.name: Oak Shield
items.description: Painted with the white ash of Greenhollow.

items.name: Steel Dagger
items.description: Narrow, quick and easy to hide. Favoured by people who do not want a fair fight.

items.name: Woodcutter's Axe
items.description: Made for oak, but it does not much care what it bites. Needs both hands.

items.name: Vale Greatsword
items.description: As long as a tall man's reach. Slow to swing and slow to stop.

items.name: Iron Helm
items.description: A riveted pot helm with a nose guard. Rings like a bell when struck.

items.name: Mail Hauberk
items.description: Ten thousand rings, each one closed by hand. Heavy on the shoulders, kind to the ribs.

items.name: Work Gloves
items.description: Thick hide gloves, scorched at the fingertips.

items.name: Smith's Gauntlets
items.description: Plated across the knuckles, for holding hot work and taking hard knocks.

items.name: Leather Leggings
items.description: Oiled against the wet and laced to the knee.

items.name: Travelling Boots
items.description: Double-soled and already broken in. The road feels shorter in them.

items.name: Iron Greaves
items.description: Shin plates on stout boots. Nothing bites through them.

items.name: White Ash Charm
items.description: A leaf of the founders' ash sealed in beeswax. It steadies the mind.

items.name: Silver Ring
items.description: Plain silver, well polished. People notice it.

items.name: Tusk Talisman
items.description: A boar tusk bound in copper wire. Hunters wear them for nerve.

items.name: Silverrun Stone
items.description: A river-worn pebble with a hole clean through it. Said to keep a traveller on their feet.

items.name: Scholar's Lens
items.description: A ground crystal on a cord. Small print and small lies both come clear through it.

races.name: Valefolk
races.description: Hardy farmers and crafters of the vale. Balanced in all things.

races.name: Ashen Elf
races.description: Long-lived wanderers with a gift for the arcane.

races.name: Stoneborn
races.description: Broad miners from under the Greybacks. Tireless.

backgrounds.name: Smith's Apprentice
backgrounds.description: You swept Bram's forge for two winters.

backgrounds.name: Woodsman
backgrounds.description: You know every deer trail in the Whisper Woods.

backgrounds.name: Wanderer
backgrounds.description: A stranger on the road with coin and questions.

npcs.name: Bram
npcs.greeting: Mind the sparks. What do you need hammered?

npcs.name: Elsa
npcs.greeting: Sit, sit. The stew is still warm.

npcs.name: Tomas
npcs.greeting: Quiet. You will scare everything from here to the river.

npcs.name: Mira
npcs.greeting: Do not touch the blue jar. Or the green one.

npcs.name: Oswin
npcs.greeting: Everything has a price, friend. Mine are merely fair.

npcs.name: Aunt Hilde
npcs.greeting: You look thin. Are you eating?

npcs.name: Cousin Wyl
npcs.greeting: Heading to the woods? Take me along next time!

npcs.name: Garrick
npcs.greeting: Still playing at swords? Stay off my trails.

npcs.name: Isolde
npcs.greeting: Stand still. That sleeve is a disgrace.

npcs.name: Petra
npcs.greeting: Papa says I am not to trouble the forge.

creatures.name: Grey Wolf
creatures.description: Lean grey hunters of the Whisper Woods. They circle before they bite, and they seldom hunt alone.

creatures.name: Tusker Boar
creatures.description: Short-tempered and thick-skulled. A tusker charges first and thinks never.

creatures.name: Vale Deer
creatures.description: Shy grazers of the meadow. They bolt at a snapped twig, so come at them from downwind.

locations.name: Greenhollow
locations.description: A ring of timbered houses around the square and the Old Well, with a gate to the north and one to the south.

locations.name: Greenhollow Road
locations.description: The cart road south of the village. Every traveller to the vale arrives by it.

locations.name: Whisper Woods
locations.description: Old trees west of the road, named for the sound the wind makes in them. Wolf country.

locations.name: Tusker Thicket
locations.description: Bramble and scrub oak east of the village, rooted up by the boar that give it its name.

locations.name: Stag Meadow
locations.description: Open grass to the south-east where the deer herds bed down. The hunters work it at dawn.

locations.name: Silverrun River
locations.description: The cold river north of the village. Trout in the shallows, yarrow on the banks.

locations.name: Greyback Dig
locations.description: A scar of red earth where the miners still cut ore from the foot of the Greybacks.

interactables.name: the notice board
interactables.text:
NOTICES OF GREENHOLLOW

WOLVES. Keep children and goats inside the gates after dusk. By order of the hunters.

ORE WANTED. Bram at the smithy pays in good bar iron for red ore from the Greybacks.

LOST. One strongbox, iron-bound, somewhere in the Silverrun. A reward to the finder, says the peddler, though the peddler has not been seen since.

interactables.name: the gate post
interactables.text:
GREENHOLLOW

Founded beneath the white ash.
Travellers welcome. Swords sheathed inside the gate.

interactables.name: the old milestone
interactables.text: The stone is older than the village. One face reads GREENHOLLOW, half a league. Another, almost worn away, points west to THE GREYBACK WORKS and has been deliberately chiselled across.

interactables.name: Mira's herbal
interactables.text:
A COMMON HERBAL, copied in Mira's hand and chained to the lectern.

YARROW. White flower, feathered leaf. Crush and bind to a wound. Best gathered where the ground stays wet.

Three sprigs steeped overnight make one draught. Bring them fresh and I will do the steeping.

Do not eat anything from this book on the strength of a drawing.

interactables.name: the wayside shrine
interactables.prompt: Rest a moment at the wayside shrine
interactables.text: A cairn of river stones under a sapling ash. Travellers leave a pebble and take a breath. You do the same, and your head feels clearer.

rumours.title: The sealed gallery
rumours.text: The founders of Greenhollow fled the Greyback mines, and the deepest gallery was sealed in a single night. Nobody wrote down why.

rumours.title: A second seam
rumours.text: The miners whisper of a richer seam somewhere under the old dig. Dunstan knows more than he says.

rumours.title: Wolves at the wood's edge
rumours.text: The wolves have come down early this year. They are seen along the edge of the Whisper Woods after dusk.

rumours.title: The white stag
rumours.text: A white stag has been seen on the meadow at dawn. Garrick swears to it, and Garrick does not like to be laughed at.

rumours.title: Boar in the thicket
rumours.text: Big boar root in the thicket east of the village. Their tusks fetch a fair price, if you come back with them.

rumours.title: The peddler's strongbox
rumours.text: A peddler lost a strongbox fording the Silverrun last spring. It should still lie somewhere near the fishing bank.

rumours.title: Yarrow on the north bank
rumours.text: The best yarrow grows where the ground stays wet, on the bank of the Silverrun north of the village.

rumours.title: Unclaimed iron
rumours.text: There is iron lying open in the hills north-east of the village, past the thicket. Nobody claims it.

rumours.title: The hunters' cache
rumours.text: The hunters keep a lean-to on Stag Meadow with a cot and a cache. Anyone caught out at night may use it, so long as they leave it tidy.

nodes.text: Mind the sparks, {player}. What do you need hammered?

lines.text: Say your piece and mind the anvil.
Good to see you, {player}. The forge burns a little brighter for company.
The forge is banked for the night, {player}. Make it quick.

replies.answer: Ingots on the left, finished work on the right. Touch nothing that glows.

replies.text: What do the miners say about the Greybacks?
replies.answer: Dunstan swears there is a second seam under the old dig, richer than the first. He will not say where. Miners.
Ha. You have stopped burning the steel, at least. Here. These were mine when I was your size.

nodes.text: Bring me red ore from the Greybacks and I will pay in bar iron. Three lumps, two bars. Fair?

replies.answer: Good red ore. Two bars, as promised. Bring more and the offer stands.

replies.text: I will keep an eye out.
replies.answer: Do. The pile is low.

nodes.text: Sit, sit. The stew is still warm.

lines.text: Evening, {player}. The common room is loud tonight. Find a stool.

replies.answer: Stag stew, barley loaf, and apples if you must be virtuous.
On the house. Do not tell Oswin, he will want one too.
Tomas says the wolves have come down to the wood's edge early this year. Keep to the road after dusk.
A peddler lost a strongbox fording the Silverrun last spring. Never found it. Near the fishing bank, he said.
Garrick came in swearing he saw a white stag on the meadow. He was three cups deep, mind.
Suit yourself. There will be more tomorrow.

nodes.text: Quiet. You will scare everything from here to the river.

lines.text: You again. Keep your voice down.

replies.answer: Boar, in the thicket east of the village. Big ones. Do not go with a knife.
Look for bent grass, not prints. Prints lie. Grass does not. And stay downwind, always.

replies.text: I brought you a wolf pelt.
replies.answer: Clean cut. Sixteen, and my thanks. One less at the wood's edge.

replies.text: May I use the lean-to on the meadow?
replies.answer: Anyone may. There is a cot, and a cache we keep stocked. Take what you need and leave it tidy.

nodes.text: Do not touch the blue jar. Or the green one.

lines.text: The shop is shut. Unless somebody is bleeding?

replies.answer: Draughts for the body, tonics for the head. Do not mix them.
It staunches bleeding. The best of it grows on the bank of the Silverrun, where the ground stays wet.

replies.text: Could you teach me a little of the craft?
replies.answer: You ask better questions than most. Mending is attention, nothing more. Hold the hurt in your mind and do not look away.

nodes.text: Always. Three fresh sprigs of yarrow and I will give you a draught for them.

replies.answer: Fresh. Good. One draught, already steeped.
I will be here. I am always here.

nodes.text: Everything has a price, friend. Mine are merely fair.

replies.answer: Look freely. Looking is the only thing I do not charge for.

replies.text: Can you do better on price?
Where do your goods come from?
replies.answer: Carters, mostly. One told me there is iron lying open in the hills north-east, past the thicket. Nobody claims it. Nobody sensible goes there, either.

nodes.text: Better? These prices are already a kindness.

replies.answer: Hm. You are, at that. I shall remember it at the till.

replies.text: A little silver for your trouble. (20 gold)
replies.answer: Now that is a language I speak fluently.
As you like. The prices will still be here.

nodes.text: You look thin. Are you eating?

lines.text: You should be abed, {player}. The cot by the door is yours, you know that.

replies.answer: I knew it. Take these, and do not argue with me.
The cot by the door is always yours. Family does not ask.

nodes.text: The barley is in, but the apples are dropping faster than I can gather them.

replies.answer: Bless you. Here, a few coppers, and do not tell me you will not take them.
Seven families came down from the Greyback mines, my grandmother's among them. They sealed the deep gallery behind them in one night. She never would say why.
Come by for supper.

nodes.text: Heading to the woods? Take me along next time!

replies.text: Come to the woods with me.
replies.answer: Aunt Hilde would skin us both. ...Next time?

nodes.text: Which one? I know two good ones.

replies.answer: It comes to the meadow at dawn, white as milk, and no arrow has ever touched it. Garrick has seen it. He goes red if you ask.
There is a second seam under the old dig. The miners found it and covered it up again. That is what I heard, anyway.
You always say that.

nodes.text: Still playing at swords? Stay off my trails.

lines.text: Hm. You again. ...Sit, if you must.

replies.text: I did not come to quarrel.
replies.answer: No? Then you are smarter than you look.

replies.text: A drink to mend things? (8 gold)
replies.answer: ...One drink. And you are buying the second.
Ha! Big words. East side of the meadow, at dawn. That is where the white one shows. Prove it.

lines.text: You. Hm. You are not as soft as you look.

replies.text: What is under the old dig?
replies.answer: A seam. A good one. And something past it that made my father put his pick down and never lift it again. Leave it be.
Hmph. With arms like that, maybe you can. Take these. You will wreck your hands otherwise.
Eight for the pair. Bram would cheat you worse.

nodes.text: Stand still. That sleeve is a disgrace.

replies.answer: There. Now you look like someone's child instead of someone's scarecrow.

replies.text: I have a hide for you.
replies.answer: Supple. Twelve, and bring me more like it.

replies.text: Make me something to walk in. (2 hides, 10 gold)
replies.answer: I had a pair cut already. A few stitches... there. Walk gently for a day.

lines.text: Nothing rises this late. Go home.

replies.answer: Fresh out of the Silverrun. Mind the bones.
Something iron-bound, down by the bank west of the ford. My line snagged it twice. Too heavy to land.
